description: Bounding VA range of the entire WGMMA intrinsic infrastructure region in ptxas .rodata

WGMMA scheduler tuning struct (pipeline_depth=32, max_pending=128, 8 stage latencies=24, special_latency=300, max_pipeline_length=1000) followed by a 22-slot handler vtable (vtable_va=0x229C4C0), 7 opcode_indices [44,45,43,54,53,52,...] and an 18-entry enum_config selecting per-stage behavior

150 function pointers into .text — the instruction-selection lowering handlers invoked when the WGMMA opcode dispatcher resolves a wgmma/mma intrinsic to a SASS sequence (all 150 slots are text pointers)

10 "Potential Performance Loss: wgmma.mma_async instructions are serialized due to ..." printf templates emitted when the pipeline builder cannot keep WGMMA async pipelines overlapped (extern calls, fn-boundary crossing, register pressure, accumulator hazards, divergent WG.DP/WG.AR)
74-entry table of 8-byte pointers (mostly into 0xACE000 .text/.rodata) — per-shape/per-type WGMMA configuration descriptors consumed by the lowering handlers

469 function pointers into .text mapping each WGMMA-family intrinsic id to its emit handler; 469 are text pointers. Handlers cluster into 15 .text neighborhoods (e.g. 0x85A000:55, 0x868000:44, 0x7D7000:38) reflecting handler groups by shape/dtype

19 vtables for WGMMA operand-type descriptor classes; most have 11 virtual slots pointing into 0xAE5xxx .text (type-classification / validation methods); first table holds packed bitfield descriptors not text pointers
39-entry table of pointers, all pointing at the same 0x21CDA50 placeholder ("???") — the human-readable WGMMA intrinsic type-name strings are not present/named in this stripped binary
739-entry switch jump table (738 nonzero) with 128 unique targets; default target 0xAEA750 hit 270 times — the main WGMMA opcode->handler dispatch switch lowered as a computed-goto table

100 small u32 arrays enumerating Mercury (internal IR) opcode ids grouped per WGMMA operation/shape; values range from small ints (8-122) up to ~2800-2930, i.e. dense opcode-id sets the dispatcher maps over
